title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is only a heading, written in the upper-right corner of an otherwise blank leaf numbered 9: "degrés de transcendance liés aux filtrations et bigraduations (comparaison de Betti, De Rham, Hodge)". It announces the programme carried out on the next page (10).

The setting, in modern terms: take a Tannakian category of motives over a number field k (or a field of finite type) with three fibre functors.
- T_B is the Betti realization, over Q.
- T_DR is the de Rham realization, over k, carrying the Hodge filtration.
- T_Hdg is a 'Hodge' fibre functor, over k. It is essentially gr_F of T_DR, i.e. the realization with its (bi)grading, tied to a splitting of the filtration by a Levi subgroup.

Pairwise Isom-torsors connect them:
- P = Isom(T_B⊗k, T_DR);
- P' = Isom(T_DR, T_Hdg), which contains Q, the bundle of Levi subgroups of the parabolic B' fixing the Hodge filtration;
- P'' = Isom(T_Hdg, T_B⊗k).

The complex points are the comparison isomorphisms α, β, γ, with βα = γ^{-1}.

The question: what are the transcendence degrees of the fields generated by
- α (the classical periods);
- β (the choice of splitting/grading);
- φ, the point of the flag variety Fil = Filt_⊗(T_B) defined over Q, i.e. the Hodge filtration written in Betti coordinates;
- ψ, the corresponding point of the variety of ⊗-bigradings Big.

The next page states a 'strong transcendence conjecture': for k ⊂ Q̄, tr.deg K/k = g + u. Here g = dim G, the motivic Galois group, and u = dim of the unipotent radical U' of B'. It deduces the following.
- tr.deg k(α)/k = g. This is Grothendieck's period conjecture.
- tr.deg Q(φ)/Q = g − b = dim G/B'. The Hodge filtration in Betti coordinates is as transcendental as the flag variety allows.
- tr.deg Q(ψ)/Q = g − l. This is the analogous statement for the Hodge bigrading.

Sanity check: for CM motives G is a torus, so B' = G and g − b = 0. The Hodge filtration is then algebraic in Betti coordinates, consistent with special points. This page itself contains no mathematics beyond the title.

ideas.what: Programme of computing transcendence degrees of the fields generated by the comparison isomorphisms Betti/de Rham/Hodge-graded, and by the Hodge filtration and Hodge bigrading viewed as points of flag/grading varieties over Q
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period conjecture (motivic Galois group torsor of periods) and its consequence for transcendence of the Hodge filtration point in a period domain/flag variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, reported in Lang 1966 and later André); Hodge-theoretic transcendence refinements in work of André, Bost–Charles and others
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture known via Lang's Introduction to Transcendental Numbers footnote and Récoltes et Semailles mentions; the filtration/bigrading refinement is not known to be published by Grothendieck

missed.claim: The heading announces extending the period conjecture from the Betti–de Rham torsor to a triangle of torsors including a 'Hodge' (graded) fibre functor. From this one gets predicted transcendence degrees g−b for the Hodge filtration point and g−l for the Hodge bigrading point, both defined over Q. This explicit triangular formulation, with the bigrading variety, is not standard in the literature, though it follows from the period conjecture.
missed.quote: degrés de transcendance liés aux filtrations et bigraduations (comparaison de Betti, De Rham, Hodge)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives precise transcendence predictions for Hodge filtrations and splittings in Betti coordinates. These are relevant to Ax–Schanuel/o-minimal transcendence results for period maps and to Bost–Charles style work. The actual content is on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only a title. Its interest lies in announcing the next page's refinement of the period conjecture to filtrations and bigradings, which is a modest, natural extension.
